summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: This Layer 1B pass maps direct public-company exposure to the defense-prime and program-integrator node. The reference lane is anchored by large primes that convert appropriations into long-cycle procurement pull-through and set supplier qualification requirements. The discovery lane emphasizes smaller or less-index-dominant public integrators/prime-adjacent firms where exposure to Navy shipbuilding, cyber, EW, mission systems, or government IT may be more specific but still needs program-level validation. External evidence supports the broader chokepoint: tariffs have been muted for major primes due to national-security exemptions, while smaller lower-tier suppliers face higher administrative burdens and weaker supply-chain visibility. Expanded the universe around defense primes as procurement-spec gatekeepers, not as the main alpha pool. The reference lane keeps Lockheed Martin as an anchor because primes convert appropriations into programs and set qualification requirements. The underfollowed lane emphasizes scarce lower-tier suppliers exposed to prime outsourcing, mission-critical electronics, engineered aerostructures, and regulated/strategic materials where small suppliers may face higher administrative burden from tariffs, exemptions, qualification, and supply-chain visibility gaps.
